channel.title: Versatile on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Versatile on Best of AI

item.title: Fauna
item.description:
Fauna set out to give developers a database that scaled globally without managing servers. It combined a flexible document model with relational features, offered strong consistency across regions, and was accessed through an API with its own query language, FQL, and earlier through GraphQL. Developers built web and mobile apps on it without running infrastructure.

The company announced that it would wind down its hosted service, and the service closed, with accounts deleted afterward. It also said it would release parts of its technology as open source, so some of the ideas may live on in community projects.

item.title: Intrinsic
item.description:
Intrinsic works on a long-standing challenge in manufacturing: robots are powerful, but programming them is slow, specialized, and expensive. The company develops a software platform that lets developers build robotic applications, using skills and tools that can be reused across different robots and tasks. The idea is similar to how an operating system and app tools made computers easier to program for a wide range of hardware.

AI and simulation play a central role. Perception tools help robots see and understand objects, motion planning handles collisions, and simulation lets teams test and refine an application virtually before running it on the factory floor. Intrinsic works with robot makers and system integrators, and it has explored combining its platform with advanced AI models so that robots can handle more varied tasks without extensive reprogramming.

item.title: Airtable
item.description: Airtable looks like a spreadsheet but behaves like a database. Records live in tables with typed fields such as dates, attachments, checkboxes, and links to records in other tables, which allows relationships that spreadsheets cannot handle. The same data can be shown as a grid, kanban board, calendar, gallery, or timeline, and filters and groups tailor each view. It’s used for content calendars, product roadmaps, CRM, event planning, and operations.

item.title: Anytype
item.description:
Anytype is a workspace for notes and structured information built around privacy. Data is stored locally and encrypted, and syncs between devices peer to peer or through backup nodes, so you keep ownership of your content rather than leaving it on a company server. The app is open source.

Its model uses objects and types. Everything is an object, such as a page, a person, a book, or a task, and each type has fields. Objects link to each other and appear in sets and collections, which function like databases. This lets users create a personal wiki or a custom organizer without code. Optional AI features can summarize and help write.

item.title: Clockwise
item.description:
Clockwise worked inside Google Calendar and Slack to protect time for deep work. It looked at a team’s calendars, moved flexible meetings, and combined scattered gaps into longer blocks, aiming to cut the constant switching between tasks that fragments a workday. It could also find meeting times that worked for groups.

The product grew a following among engineering and product teams, and added AI scheduling features and a way to plan work around priorities. The company ended the service and the team joined Salesforce, where they work on AI agents. The product itself did not move over.

item.title: HiBob
item.description:
HiBob is built for companies that want a modern HR system for distributed teams. It stores employee records, handles onboarding and time off, supports performance reviews, and manages compensation and benefits. The interface is designed for employees as well as HR, with a social feel and company-wide features.

Analytics and AI help leaders. Compensation benchmarking compares pay with market data, workforce planning tools model headcount, and an assistant answers HR questions and drafts documents. Payroll integrations and a marketplace of apps connect Bob with finance and IT systems.

item.title: Notion
item.description:
Notion lets people build their own workspace from simple pieces. A page can hold text, headings, checklists, images, embedded files, and databases, and databases can be shown as tables, boards, calendars, or galleries. Teams use it for wikis, meeting notes, project tracking, product roadmaps, and personal organization, and templates help people get started. Real-time collaboration, comments, and permissions make it work for teams as well as individuals.

The product has grown beyond notes. Notion Calendar and Notion Mail connect scheduling and email to the workspace, and Sites turns pages into public web pages. Notion AI adds writing help, summaries, translation, and question answering across your workspace and connected tools like Slack and Google Drive, plus agents that perform tasks. AI meeting notes capture and summarize calls. See the Notion AI entry for details on those features.

item.title: WooCommerce
item.description:
WooCommerce is the most widely used way to run a store on WordPress. You install the plugin, add products, set up payments, shipping, and taxes, and manage orders from the WordPress dashboard. Because it is open source, you own the store and the data, host it where you want, and can modify anything with code or extensions.

The ecosystem is its strength. Thousands of themes and extensions add subscriptions, bookings, memberships, marketplaces, and connections to accounting and marketing tools. AI extensions can write product descriptions, suggest recommendations, and help with support, and Automattic’s own tools plus third-party plugins fill the gaps. Many agencies build custom stores on top of it.

item.title: Notion
item.description: Notion works as a set of building blocks. A team can create a company wiki, a project tracker with a board view, a product roadmap, a meeting notes database, and a documentation site, all in one workspace with permissions and comments. Databases are central: the same set of records can be viewed as a table, board, calendar, or timeline, and linked to other databases, which makes it possible to build custom systems without code.
